case.case_title: Kanapathipilli vs. Sri Lanka Broadcasting Corporation and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC 145/2007, decided on 22 January 2009

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the appointment of the 4th respondent to the post of Director Tamil Service violated Article 12(1) of the Constitution by discriminating against the petitioner.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that the 4th respondent was disqualified from re-employment under Administrative Circular 44/90 and that the petitioner had scored the highest marks among eligible candidates, making the appointment illegal and discriminatory under Article 12(1).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents contended that the Corporation was unaware of the 4th respondent’s disqualification, the interviews were held over two years ago, and the petitioner’s marks did not reflect an extremely high degree of competence.
key_facts: The 4th respondent was disqualified from re-employment under Public Administration Circular No. 44/90.
The petitioner scored 42 marks and the 4th respondent scored 48 marks at the interview.
The 4th respondent was under interdiction for fraud but reinstated after repayment.
The 4th respondent was appointed despite disqualification.
The petitioner was qualified and had nearly 12 years of experience as a Programme Producer.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court held that equality under Article 12(1) means that equals must be treated equally and unequals unequally. Since the 4th respondent was disqualified, he and the petitioner were not equals and could not be treated as such. The appointment of the 4th respondent was arbitrary, unreasonable, and violated the petitioner’s fundamental rights under Article 12(1).
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court found that the 4th respondent should not have been called for the interview due to disqualification, making the petitioner the only qualified candidate. Therefore, the appointment of the 4th respondent was invalid and discriminatory against the petitioner.
principles_established: Equality requires treating equals equally and unequals unequally.
Disqualification under administrative rules affects equality in appointment.
Appointments must be reasonable and justifiable to comply with Article 12(1).
precedents_cited: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
M. K. Wijetunga et al v. The Principal, Southlands College
Asanka Pathiratne v. University Grants Commission
Anushka Jayatileke v. University Grants Commission
Samarasinghe v. Air Lanka and others

outcome.holding: The Court held that the appointment of the 4th respondent violated Article 12(1) and was invalid. The petitioner’s fundamental rights were infringed. The appointment of the 4th respondent was to be terminated and the petitioner was awarded compensation.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The appointment of the 4th respondent was terminated forthwith. The petitioner was awarded Rs. 100,000 as compensation and costs. The 1st respondent was directed to fill the vacancy in accordance with its policy within four months.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the Court’s reasoning as it protects equality before the law and prohibits arbitrary discrimination in public appointments. The Court applied this clause directly to invalidate the appointment and uphold the petitioner’s rights.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Court found that the 4th respondent was disqualified under Administrative Circular 44/90 and thus could not be treated as equal to the petitioner, making the appointment arbitrary and violative of Article 12(1).
